close_reason: Separate inline comments added to sortAsTree and filterAsTree rejection arms explaining explicit-rejection rationale per RFC 8621 §2.3
description: In handle_mailbox_query, when sortAsTree=true or filterAsTree=true, the handler returns unsupportedSort or unsupportedFilter rather than silently ignoring the flag and returning flat results. A contributor might remove these checks as overly defensive, since the result 'looks' fine without tree traversal. But silently ignoring sortAsTree/filterAsTree would produce semantically wrong results for clients that rely on tree-mode semantics — e.g. filterAsTree affects whether child mailboxes are included based on parent match. Failing loudly with the correct RFC 8620 error is strictly better than silently returning wrong data.
title: Mailbox/query sortAsTree/filterAsTree explicitly rejected with unsupportedSort/unsupportedFilter rather than silently ignored
